sections.html:
Jackson is the seat of Jackson County, so a sale here passes through two sets of offices. City hall on West Michigan Avenue deals with assessing, treasury and rental registration, while the county records the deed. Whether you list with an agent, find a buyer yourself or accept an as-is cash offer, closing follows the same legal steps. The real differences are the shape the house is in and who lives there.

Jackson sits at the junction of I-94 and US 127, roughly 35 miles west of Ann Arbor, 35 miles south of Lansing, 75 miles west of Detroit and 65 miles east of Kalamazoo. The mid-2025 population estimate is 31,022, a 0.9 percent slip from the 2020 base.

Survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show a low-cost market:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $103,200.
  • Homeownership: 54.7 percent of 13,281 households.
  • Typical rent: $898 a month.
  • Average trip to work: 17.0 minutes.

With a typical value near $103,000 and almost half of households renting, many Jackson houses belong to investors or need repairs. Expect buyers to inspect the roof, furnace and foundation closely. Winters are cold, with a January low averaging 17.5 degrees and about 37.3 inches of snow a year, so a sound furnace and roof are real selling points. If repair costs would run higher than what they add to the price, an as-is sale to a cash buyer may be the simpler path.

Jackson keeps a registry of rentals that are not owner-occupied, and a sale restarts it. A registration is good for 3 years, owners report changes within 10 days, and renewals are due no later than 60 days before expiry. Selling voids the registration, and the new owner applies at closing. Within 45 days after the sale, the seller of a rented dwelling tells the Community Development Department who bought it and where to reach them.

A buyer who claims a 100 percent principal residence exemption with the city assessor skips registration. Anyone else registers within 45 days of closing, with a $5 per unit daily penalty for lateness. Fees are not refunded or credited on a transfer, so a seller who just paid for a registration cannot recover it.

If you own a rental, tell your buyer about the registration rules before the offer is final. An investor who plans to keep the tenants needs to know the paperwork starts over on their side.

sections.h2: Due dates and the assessing calendar
sections.html:
City bills arrive July 1 (summer) and December 1 (winter). Pay the summer bill in one lump by July 31, or split it into five payments due on the 20th from July to November. The winter bill is open for payment December 1 to February 14. The assessor's calendar sets the rest of the year:

Jackson assessing calendar for a property owner
DateWhat happens
February 14Final penalty-free day for last year's winter bill
Second week of MarchAssessment appeals heard by the Board of Review
June 1Principal residence exemption claims due
July 31Summer bill due; last day for a residential Tax Tribunal appeal following a March Board of Review appeal
December 31Tax day: condition of the property on this date sets the next assessment

Ask the treasurer's office for a payoff figure before closing so your title company can settle whatever is still open.

sections.h2: Why will a buyer's Jackson tax bill likely exceed mine?
sections.html:
Taxable value on a Michigan home can climb only by the lesser of 5 percent or inflation each year while one owner holds it. A sale ends that cap. Under MCL 211.27a, the next calendar year's taxable value jumps to the state equalized value, roughly half of market value. Someone who has owned for decades pays far less than the person who buys from them, so tell serious buyers early while they are still comparing monthly costs.

You also have a form to file. Once you move out, rescind your principal residence exemption within 90 days (MCL 211.7cc) and send it to the Jackson assessor.

sections.h2: City income tax after you sell
sections.html: Jackson levies its own income tax. Residents with income over $600 file and pay 1 percent. People who commute in to work pay 0.5 percent, and corporations and partnerships pay 1 percent. Returns are due April 30, moving to Monday if the date falls on a weekend. If you sell and move out of town, ask the treasurer's office how a part-year return works.

The seller owes two Michigan transfer taxes when the deed is recorded. The state rate is $3.75 for each $500 of price. The county adds 55 cents for each $500, a rate that applies to counties under 2,000,000 residents. At the Jackson County Register of Deeds you can combine the tax and the recording fee in one check made out to that office.

MCL 207.526 exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, title-correction deeds and security instruments, and the county register posts its own exemption guidance. Your title agent should show every line on the settlement statement so nothing surprises you at the table. Bring your deed and a photo ID to the title office, and ask whether the buyer or the seller covers the recording fee in your contract.

Buyers who commute to Lansing, Ann Arbor or Detroit weigh the drive on I-94 and US 127, so state the exit and the drive time to each in your listing. Local landmarks give buyers a sense of the place:

  • Dawn Foods, family-owned, has been based in Jackson since 1920.
  • Reynolds Field, a general aviation airport of about 700 acres south of I-94, hosts the Jackson College Flight School and the annual Jackson Blues Festival in June.
  • The city's parks department runs 26 parks totaling 645 acres, and JATA buses run ten routes Monday through Saturday from a downtown station.

Almost the whole city lies inside Jackson Public Schools. Mention the district when buyers ask.

sections.h2: Steps for a cash sale or a listing
sections.html:
Any route to closing starts with the same homework. Dig out your newest summer and winter tax bills. Look through your records for any past rental registration. Settle who will pay for repairs. Then get a draft settlement statement from your title agent with the transfer tax shown. A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiations that often follow a buyer's inspection, and it lets you pick the closing date.

After closing, rescind your homestead exemption within 90 days if the house was your principal residence, and let Community Development know if tenants lived there.

faqs.q: What must a Jackson landlord tell the city after a sale?
faqs.a: Send Community Development the buyer's name and contact details within 45 days of the sale. The buyer then has 45 days from closing to register, unless they file for a 100 percent principal residence exemption.

faqs.q: When are Jackson summer property taxes due?
faqs.a: Either all at once by July 31 or in five installments on the 20th of each month from July to November. The winter bill can be paid from December 1 until February 14.
Yes. Residents with more than $600 in income pay 1 percent and nonresident workers pay 0.5 percent, with returns due April 30.

faqs.q: What transfer tax does a Jackson seller pay?
faqs.a: The seller covers a state tax of $3.75 per $500 of price plus a county tax of 55 cents per $500. Both are due when the deed is recorded, and one check to the Register of Deeds can cover tax and fee together.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a new Jackson owner's principal residence exemption?
faqs.a: The claim is due June 1 to cover the summer bill, and the buyer needs to own and live in the house by that date. A missed claim can still be fixed at the July Board of Review.
